C: A1 one of the two organs in your face that are used for seeing
› a dark spot on a potato or similar plant part, from which a new stem and leaves will grow
（馬鈴薯或者類似植物的）芽眼
› the hole in a needle through which you put the thread

NONE: › to look at someone or something with interest
（有興趣地）看，注視

example: He has no sight in his left eye.
他左眼失明。
She's got beautiful green eyes.
她有一對漂亮的綠色眼睛。
He closed his eyes and went to sleep.
他闔上眼睡了。
I could see her eyeing my lunch.
我看到她像很有興趣地看著我的午飯。
She eyed me warily.
她警惕地看著我。

NONE: › someone or something that is attractive but not very interesting or useful
華而不實的人（或物）

example: Most of the images on the website are not more than eye candy.
網頁上大多數圖片雖然很有吸引力，但卻毫無意義。

NONE: C2 the situation in which two people look at each other's eyes at the same time
目光接觸

example: He's very shy and never makes eye contact.
他很靦腆，從不與別人有目光接觸。
If you're telling the truth, why are you avoiding eye contact with me?
如果你說的是實話，為甚麼不敢看我的眼睛？

NONE: › If something is at eye level, it is positioned at approximately the same height as your eyes.
視線高度，齊眼高度
› to look at someone with sexual interest
向…眉目傳情，向…送秋波，向…拋媚眼

example: That guy in the grey jacket has been eyeing you up all evening.
那個穿灰夾克的小子整晚都在色瞇瞇地看著你。

NONE: › a coloured cream or powder that is put around the eyes to make them look larger or more attractive
眼影，眼影膏
› one of the two round, low areas on each side of the nose that contain the eyes
眼窩
› to look closely at something that you are interested in
很有興趣地仔細看

example: I saw you eyeing up that chocolate cake.
我看到你的眼死盯著那塊巧克力蛋糕。

NONE: › very attractive or noticeable
引人注目的，搶眼的，惹人注意的

example: an eye-catching poster
引人注目的海報

NONE: › something that surprises you and teaches you new facts about life, people, etc.
使人大開眼界的事物；有啟發性的東西

example: Living in another country can be a real eye-opener.
在外國生活確實可以令人大開眼界。

NONE: › the whole eye, including the part that cannot usually be seen
眼球
› to look closely at someone
注視；盯；仔細打量

example: He eyeballed me across the bar.
他在酒吧的另一邊看著我。

NONE: › If you are eyeball to eyeball with an enemy or someone you are arguing with, you deal with them in a direct way.
面對面地；怒目相向地；劍拔弩張地
B2 the line of short hairs above each eye in humans
眉，眉毛

example: Do you pluck your eyebrows (= remove some of the hairs to change their shape)?
你修眉毛嗎？
He's got really bushy (= thick) eyebrows.
他的眉毛很濃。

NONE: › with the type of eyes described
長著…眼睛的

example: a brown-eyed baby girl
長著褐色眼睛的女嬰
She was wide-eyed in amazement.
她吃驚得睜大了雙眼。

C: › [ C ] an amount of something, usually dust or dirt, that has entered the eye
S: › [ S ] informal a very noticeable or attractive sight, often a sexually attractive person
賞心悅目的景象；好看的人（或物）

example: As the lorry went past, I got an eyeful of grit.
貨車開過去的時候，我被弄得一眼的沙子。
She's quite an eyeful.
她真是個美人。

NONE: glass noun(FOR IMPROVING SIGHT)
› a hole that you can look through
（門或牆上的）窺視孔

example: Ensure the eyeholes in the mask are large enough.
確保面具上的眼洞足夠大。

NONE: › present participle of
eye verb
B2 any of the short hairs that grow along the edges of the eye
睫毛

example: long eyelashes
長長的睫毛
false eyelashes
假睫毛

NONE: › a small hole in material, the edge of which is protected by a ring of metal, through which a piece of string, a shoelace, etc. is put to fasten something
（周邊嵌有金屬環，供穿繩固定用的）孔眼
› a small hole with thread around the edge as part of a design used to decorate material
（裝飾用）鑲邊小圓孔

example: an eyelet bedspread
一張裝飾著鑲邊小圓孔的床單

NONE: B2 either of the two pieces of skin that can close over each eye
眼瞼，眼皮
› a coloured substance, usually contained in a pencil, that is put in a line just above or below the eyes in order to make them look more attractive
眼線液；眼線筆
› a covering worn over the eye to protect it if it is damaged or sore
眼罩
› the part of a piece of equipment, for example, a microscope, through which you look
（顯微鏡等儀器的）（ 接）目鏡
› If people's eyes meet, they look at each other at the same time.
目光相遇

example: Their eyes met across a crowded room.
他們身處一個擁擠的房間，兩人的目光穿過人群的縫隙，互相對視。

NONE: › If your eyes are out on stalks, they are wide open with surprise.
吃驚得瞪大了眼睛

example: His eyes were out on stalks as he watched his neighbour drive past in a brand new Porsche.
看到鄰居開著一輛嶄新的保時捷經過時，他吃驚得瞪大了眼睛。

NONE: B2 the ability to see
視力

example: good/bad/poor eyesight
視力好／不好／差

你要去檢查一下視力。

NONE: › an unpleasant or ugly sight in a public place
（公共場所的）不順眼的東西，難看的東西

example: They think the new library building is an eyesore.
他們覺得新建成的圖書館大樓不好看。

NONE: › tired or painful eyes as a result of too much reading, looking at a computer screen, etc.
眼痛；眼睛疲勞
› either of the two pointed teeth that are found one on each side of the top of the mouth
上尖牙，上犬齒

C or U: › [ C or U ] a liquid used to clean the eyes

U: › [ U ] old-fashioned informal nonsense or something that is not true

NONE: › a person who saw something happen, for example, a crime or an accident
目擊者；見證人

example: According to an eyewitness account, the thieves abandoned their vehicle near the scene of the robbery.
據一位目擊證人的描述，這幫盜賊在搶劫現場附近棄車潛逃。
